mainTopic: Saying a ברכה for others after fulfilling your own obligation; why the שופר is not blown when ראש השנה falls on שבת, and רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's enactment in יבנה
overview: The amud opens by asking about two in-between cases: the bread ברכה on מצה at the סדר and the wine ברכה of קידוש. The question is whether someone who already fulfilled his own obligation can still say these ברכות for others. רב פפי's practice of making קידוש again for his tenants shows that he can. A ברייתא then sums up the rules. Do not say the bread ברכה for guests unless you eat with them, but you may say it for your children to train them. הלל and מגילה can always be done for others. The chapter ראוהו בית דין ends, and a new פרק opens with a משנה: when ראש השנה falls on שבת, the שופר was blown only in the מקדש, and after the חורבן רבן יוחנן בן זכאי allowed it wherever there is a בית דין. The גמרא first tries to find a Torah source for not blowing on שבת. רבא rejects that source and explains that the ban is a rabbinic decree, made for fear of carrying the שופר to an expert, and that the same concern applies to לולב and מגילה. Finally, a ברייתא tells how רבן יוחנן בן זכאי established blowing in יבנה. The גמרא then shows that the חכמים differ from the תנא קמא over a temporary בית דין, and it begins a comment by רב הונא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Can you say the bread blessing on מצה or the wine blessing of קידוש for others?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the המוציא on מצה and the בורא פרי הגפן of קידוש follow the general rule (you can say them for others even after you already did) or the exception for bread and wine (only if you eat or drink).
steps.simpleTranslation: What about the blessing on the bread of מצה, and the blessing on the wine of קידוש? Since there is an obligation, can a person say them for others even after he already fulfilled his own? Or perhaps the blessing itself is not the obligation, so he cannot?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about two special cases that sit between the general rule and its exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the ברכה on bread or wine depends on your own eating or drinking, so you cannot say it for others once you are done. But eating מצה and drinking קידוש wine are a חובה. The two sides of the question are: (1) the חובה makes the ברכה part of a מצוה, so you can say it for others; or (2) the חובה is only the eating and drinking, and the ברכה itself is still just a ברכת הנהנין.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the law? (opens a question)
An obligation
He takes out (fulfills the obligation for) others
Or perhaps (introduces the other side of the question)
The sanctification of the day: קידוש on שבת or יום טוב

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether one may make קידוש for others in general. It is specifically about someone who already fulfilled his own obligation and is not eating or drinking now.

phrases.english: The blessing over the bread of matzah,
phrases.notes: The המוציא said at the סדר before eating מצה

phrases.aramaic: וּבִרְכַּת הַיַּיִן שֶׁל קִידּוּשׁ הַיּוֹם, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: and the blessing over the wine of the sanctification of the day, what is the law?
phrases.notes: The בורא פרי הגפן said as part of קידוש

phrases.english: Since it is an obligation, can he take others out?
phrases.notes: Side 1: the מצוה makes it like other ברכות

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא: בְּרָכָה לָאו חוֹבָה הִיא.
phrases.english: Or perhaps: the blessing is not the obligation.
phrases.notes: Side 2: only the eating or drinking is required, so the ברכה stays a ברכת הנהנין

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ? כֵּיוָן דְּחוֹבָה הוּא — מַפֵּיק, אוֹ דִלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier sugya (on the previous section of the daf) about אף על פי שיצא מוציא and its exception for bread and wine.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the חובה of eating מצה or drinking קידוש wine turn their ברכה into a מצוה-ברכה that can be said for others after one has already fulfilled his own obligation?

steps.title: רב פפי made קידוש again for his tenants
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reports that רב פפי made קידוש for his students, and then made it again for his tenants when they came in from the field. This shows that one may say קידוש for others even after fulfilling his own obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רב אשי said, when we were at רב פפי's house, he would make קידוש for us. And when his tenant farmers came in from the field, he would make קידוש for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a story about how רב פפי acted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפי had already made קידוש and fulfilled his obligation. Yet he made קידוש again, including the ברכה on the wine, for the tenants who came later. This shows that the wine ברכה of קידוש counts as part of the חובה, and so it can be said for others.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (introduces a source that answers the question)
The house or study hall of רב פפי
Makes קידוש
His tenant farmers (sharecroppers)
From the field

steps.whatToRemember: The ברכה on the wine of קידוש can be said for others even if you already made קידוש for yourself, because it is part of the מצוה.

phrases.english: Come and hear, for Rav Ashi said:
When we were at the house of Rav Pappi,
he would make kiddush for us.
phrases.notes: At this point רב פפי has already fulfilled his own obligation

phrases.english: And when his tenants would come from the field,
he would make kiddush for them.
phrases.notes: A second קידוש, said only for their sake

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1 with an example of how an אמורא acted.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. The wine ברכה of קידוש is treated as part of the חובה, so one may say it for others after fulfilling his own obligation.
steps.raayaObject: Whether one who already fulfilled his obligation can say the קידוש wine ברכה for others
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב אשי's report about רב פפי making קידוש a second time for his tenants

steps.title: ברייתא on breaking bread for guests, children, and on הלל and מגילה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches four rules. A person should not say the bread ברכה for guests unless he eats with them. He may say it for his children and household to train them in מצוות. For הלל and מגילה, he may lead others even after he already fulfilled his own obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: A person should not break bread for guests unless he eats with them. But he may break bread for his children and household members to train them in מצוות. And with הלל and מגילה, even if he already fulfilled his obligation, he can fulfill it for others.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that lays out where you may and may not say a ברכה or lead a מצוה for others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For guests, the bread ברכה is a ברכת הנהנין, so you must be eating yourself to say it for them. Your own children and household are an exception: training them (חינוך) is itself a מצוה for you, so you may say it for them even without eating. הלל and מגילה are pure מצוות, so the general rule of אף על פי שיצא מוציא applies to them.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught (introduces a ברייתא)
Break bread, meaning say המוציא and cut the bread for others
Guests
To train them in מצוות (חינוך)
Even though he already fulfilled his obligation, he can fulfill it for others

steps.whatToRemember: There are two kinds of ברכה here. A ברכת הנהנין (bread and wine) requires that you eat or drink yourself, except for training your own family. A מצוה like הלל or מגילה, or the מצוה part of קידוש, can be done for others even after you already fulfilled it.
steps.confusionAlert: The children case does not mean children are not covered by the ברכת הנהנין rule. It is a special exception, allowed because of the מצוה of חינוך.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A person should not break bread for guests
phrases.notes: That is, say המוציא on their behalf

phrases.english: unless he is eating with them,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל פּוֹרֵס הוּא לְבָנָיו וְלִבְנֵי בֵיתוֹ
phrases.english: but he may break bread for his children and household members
phrases.notes: Even if he is not eating

phrases.english: in order to train them in מצוות.
And with Hallel and the Megillah,
even though he already fulfilled his obligation, he can fulfill it for others.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: לָא יִפְרוֹס אָדָם פְּרוּסָה לָאוֹרְחִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that spells out the rules for saying ברכות for others, adding the חינוך exception and the cases of הלל and מגילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not say the bread ברכה for guests unless you eat with them. You may say it for your children and household to train them. For הלל and מגילה, אף על פי שיצא מוציא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practical halacha that one may not say המוציא for guests without eating, but may lead others in הלל, מגילה, or the מצוה part of a ברכה after having already fulfilled his own obligation.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing the chapter ראוהו בית דין
steps.stepSummary: The standard הדרן formula marks the end of the third פרק of ראש השנה, ראוהו בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter 'ראוהו בית דין.'
steps.whatsHappening: The chapter ends here. This line is the traditional farewell to the פרק, not a legal statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הדרן means 'we will return to you.' It expresses the learner's commitment to come back and review this chapter. The next פרק, יום טוב של ראש השנה, opens with a new משנה about blowing שופר on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (formula ending a chapter)
"The court saw it": the name of the third chapter of ראש השנה

phrases.english: We will return to you, Ra'uhu Beis Din

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַרַן עֲלָךְ רָאוּהוּ בֵּית דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the final ברייתא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter ראוהו בית דין is complete.

steps.title: New chapter: blowing שופר on שבת and the תקנה of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opening the new פרק rules that when ראש השנה falls on שבת, the שופר is blown in the מקדש but not elsewhere. After the חורבן, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי instituted blowing wherever there is a בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: When ראש השנה falls on שבת, they would blow the שופר in the מקדש, but not in the rest of the country. Once the מקדש was destroyed, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי made a rule that they should blow in any place that has a בית דין.
steps.whatsHappening: A brand-new פרק begins with a משנה. It sets the basic rule for blowing שופר when ראש השנה falls on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the שופר is blown everywhere on ראש השנה. On שבת there is an exception: only the מקדש blows. After the מקדש was gone, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי moved this special status to places with a בית דין.

keyTerms.meaning: The country outside the מקדש (everywhere else)
They blow (the שופר)
Instituted a rabbinic enactment (תקנה)
The leading sage at the time of the חורבן, who rebuilt Torah life in יבנה
A rabbinic court

steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה is the basis for the practice of not blowing שופר on שבת.

phrases.english: The festival of ראש השנה
that happened to fall on שבת —
in the מקדש they would blow the שופר,
but not in the rest of the country.
Once the בית המקדש was destroyed,
רבן יוחנן בן זכאי instituted
that they should blow in every place
that has a בית דין.

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new פרק after the הדרן in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On ראש השנה that falls on שבת, the שופר is blown only in the מקדש. After the חורבן, it is blown wherever there is a בית דין.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר limits the enactment to יבנה, and the חכמים disagree
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says the תקנה applied only to יבנה. The חכמים reply that it applies to יבנה and to any place with a בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי made this rule only for יבנה. They answered him: יבנה and every other place with a בית דין are the same.
steps.whatsHappening: Still inside the משנה, a dispute breaks out about how far the תקנה reaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר reads the תקנה narrowly: only יבנה, where the great בית דין sat, took over the מקדש's status. The חכמים say any בית דין qualifies. Their words sound like the משנה's first ruling. Steps 21-22 show that the two views actually differ over a temporary בית דין.

keyTerms.meaning: The town where the Sanhedrin moved after the חורבן
Only
They (the other sages) said to him

phrases.english: רבי אלעזר said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הִתְקִין רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
phrases.english: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי did not institute it
except in יבנה alone.
They said to him:
It is the same for יבנה and for every place
that has a בית דין.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: לֹא הִתְקִין רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי אֶלָּא בְּיַבְנֶה בִּלְבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the scope of the תקנה stated in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר limits the תקנה to יבנה. The חכמים extend it to every place with a בית דין.

steps.title: ירושלים had an advantage over יבנה
steps.stepSummary: In ירושלים, nearby towns could also blow on שבת. In יבנה, only the בית דין itself could blow.
steps.simpleTranslation: ירושלים had one more advantage over יבנה. Any town that could see ירושלים, hear the שופר from there, was close by, and could walk there would also blow the שופר. In יבנה, they blew only in the בית דין itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds one more difference, showing that ירושלים's status was wider than יבנה's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ירושלים, the right to blow on שבת reached nearby towns that met all four conditions. In יבנה, the right stayed inside the court. The תקנה was a smaller copy of the original status, not a full replacement.

keyTerms.meaning: Had an extra advantage, superior
Can see and can hear
Is close and can come

steps.whatToRemember: On שבת ראש השנה: the מקדש (and in ירושלים, nearby towns) blew. After the חורבן, a בית דין blows, but only inside the court.

phrases.english: And ירושלים had this additional feature,
superior to יבנה:
that any town that can see and can hear,
and is near, and is able to come —
they blow there.
But in יבנה they would not blow
except in the בית דין alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד זֹאת הָיְתָה יְרוּשָׁלַיִם יְתֵירָה עַל יַבְנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further contrast between ירושלים and יבנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In ירושלים, nearby towns that met the four conditions also blew. In יבנה, only the בית דין blew.

steps.title: The גמרא asks for the source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that the שופר is not blown on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its discussion by asking for the source of the משנה's rule that the שופר is not blown outside the מקדש on שבת. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumes there must be a reason why a מצוה from the Torah is set aside on שבת. The גמרא wants to know whether that reason comes from a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
From where are these words (learned)?

phrases.english: GEMARA:
From where are these matters derived?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the משנה's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for not blowing the שופר on שבת outside the מקדש.

steps.title: Two verses: remembering the blast versus blowing it
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי בר לחמא, citing רבי חמא בר חנינא, points out two פסוקים. One speaks only of 'remembering' the blast, and the other says it is a 'day of blowing.' He resolves them: the first speaks of ראש השנה on שבת, and the second of ראש השנה on a weekday.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי בר לחמא said in the name of רבי חמא בר חנינא: One פסוק says 'a rest day, a remembering of the blast.' Another says 'a day of blowing it shall be for you.' This is not a contradiction. The first is about ראש השנה that falls on שבת, and the second is about ראש השנה that falls on a weekday.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא answers the question by pointing to two פסוקים that seem to clash. He solves the clash by assigning each פסוק to a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'זכרון תרועה' sounds like only mentioning the blast, while 'יום תרועה' means actually blowing. Splitting them into שבת and weekday gives a Torah source for not blowing on שבת. The word שבתון in the first פסוק hints at the שבת connection.

keyTerms.meaning: One verse says (introduces two verses that seem to clash)
A remembering of the blast (only mentioning it)
A day of blowing
It is not difficult (the contradiction is solved)
A weekday

steps.confusionAlert: This answer makes the rule a Torah law (דאורייתא). That is exactly what רבא is about to attack.

phrases.english: רבי לוי בר לחמא said
in the name of רבי חמא בר חנינא:
One verse says:
'A solemn rest, a remembering of the blast.'
And another verse says:
'It shall be a day of blowing for you'!
It is not difficult:

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן — בְּיוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בַּשַּׁבָּת,
phrases.english: Here — when the festival falls on שבת,

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן — בְּיוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בַּחוֹל.
phrases.english: there — when the festival falls on a weekday.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּתוּב אֶחָד אוֹמֵר: שַׁבָּתוֹן זִכְרוֹן תְּרוּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8 with a derivation from פסוקים.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not blowing on שבת comes from 'זכרון תרועה,' which applies when ראש השנה falls on שבת. 'יום תרועה' applies to a weekday.

steps.title: רבא: if it is Torah law, how could they blow in the מקדש?
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects: if the Torah forbids blowing on שבת, the מקדש should not blow either.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If this is a Torah law, how do we blow in the מקדש?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges the derivation of step 9 by pointing to the משנה's own ruling about the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A Torah-level 'remember, don't blow' rule should apply everywhere, including the מקדש. The משנה says the מקדש did blow on שבת. This suggests the ban is rabbinic, since rabbinic bans did not apply in the מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: From Torah law (as opposed to rabbinic law)
How?

phrases.english: רבא said:
If it is from Torah law,
how do we blow in the מקדש?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אִי מִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא הִיא, בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ הֵיכִי תָּקְעִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the Torah-level derivation of step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The derivation of רבי לוי בר לחמא from the two פסוקים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A Torah ban would apply in the מקדש too, but the משנה says the מקדש blew on שבת.

steps.title: Second objection: blowing שופר is not a forbidden מלאכה
steps.stepSummary: רבא adds that blowing a שופר is not a forbidden מלאכה, so no פסוק is needed to exclude it on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: blowing is not a forbidden kind of work, such that a פסוק would be needed to exclude it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a second, deeper objection to the derivation. He sets up a proof that the גמרא will bring next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסוק is needed to stop a מצוה only if doing it would break a Torah ban. Blowing a שופר is not a Torah-forbidden מלאכה on שבת. So the Torah has nothing to forbid, and the derivation is unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: A forbidden act of work on שבת or יום טוב
To exclude
A verse is needed

steps.whatToRemember: רבא shows that not blowing on שבת cannot be a Torah law. The rule must be rabbinic, and the גמרא will look for its real reason.

phrases.english: And furthermore:
it is not a forbidden labor,
such that a verse would be needed to exclude it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד: הָא לָאו מְלָאכָה הִיא, דְּאִצְטְרִיךְ קְרָא לְמַעוֹטֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second objection to רבא's challenge in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for a פסוק to forbid blowing on שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Blowing a שופר is not a Torah-forbidden מלאכה, so there is nothing for a פסוק to exclude.

steps.title: Proof that blowing a שופר is a skill, not a forbidden labor
steps.stepSummary: רבא backs up his challenge with a ברייתא from the school of שמואל: the פסוק about forbidden work leaves out blowing a שופר and removing bread from the oven, because these are skills and not real labor.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the school of שמואל taught: 'You shall do no servile work.' This leaves out blowing a שופר and taking bread out of the oven, because that is a skill and not a labor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for רבא's point from Step 11: a ברייתא that says blowing a שופר is not a מלאכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא learns from the words 'מלאכת עבודה' that only real labor is forbidden on יום טוב. Blowing a שופר is a 'חכמה', a skill, not a labor. So the Torah never forbade it, and the earlier answer in Step 9 cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא taught in the study hall of שמואל
Servile work, the kind of labor the Torah forbids on יום טוב
Removing bread from the walls of the oven
A skill or know-how, as opposed to physical labor

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this ברייתא means blowing a שופר is allowed on שבת in practice. It only says that by Torah law it is not a forbidden labor. A rabbinic decree still forbids it, as the next steps explain.

phrases.english: As the school of Shmuel taught:
"You shall do no manner of servile work",
this excludes blowing a shofar
and removing bread from the oven,
since it is a skill and not a labor.
phrases.notes: Applies to both שופר blowing and removing bread.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנָא דְּבֵי שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for רבא's claim in Step 11 that blowing a shofar is not a מלאכה.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that blowing a שופר is not a forbidden labor, so no פסוק is needed to exclude it on שבת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of דבי שמואל reading 'כל מלאכת עבודה לא תעשו' as excluding skills like שופר blowing and removing bread.

steps.title: רבא's new answer: permitted by Torah law, forbidden by a rabbinic decree
steps.stepSummary: Having rejected the answer from the פסוקים, רבא gives a new answer: by Torah law blowing on שבת is fully permitted, and only the רבנן forbade it, following רבה's reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: by Torah law it is completely permitted, and it is the רבנן who made a decree against it, as רבה explained.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a brand new answer to the question of Step 8. The ban on blowing the שופר on שבת is rabbinic, not from the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אלא' (rather) tells us the earlier answer from the פסוקים is dropped. This also solves רבא's first challenge in Step 10: a rabbinic decree did not apply in the מקדש, so the מקדש could still blow. The details of the decree come in the next step from רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; signals dropping the earlier answer for a new one
By Torah law
It is completely permitted
They decreed; a rabbinic prohibition

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the halachic basis for why we do not blow the שופר on ראש השנה that falls on שבת: it is a rabbinic decree, which is why the מקדש, and later the בית דין, could be treated differently.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
By Torah law it is completely permitted,
and it is the Rabbis who decreed against it
in line with Rabba.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After proving the Torah does not forbid שופר blowing, רבא replaces the answer of Step 9 with a new one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where do we learn that the שופר is not blown on שבת? (Step 8)
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is not from the Torah at all. It is a rabbinic decree.

steps.title: רבה's reason for the decree: carrying the שופר to an expert
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains the decree: everyone must hear the שופר but not everyone knows how to blow, so a person might carry it to an expert to learn and carry it four אמות in the public domain.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבה said: everyone is obligated in blowing the שופר, but not everyone is an expert at it. So the רבנן made a decree, in case a person takes it in his hand, goes to an expert to learn, and carries it four אמות in the public domain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבה's statement to explain exactly why the רבנן forbade blowing on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blowing itself is fine. The worry is about carrying. Since many people do not know how to blow, someone might bring his שופר to an expert and, in his rush, carry it four אמות in רשות הרבים, which is a real Torah prohibition on שבת. The רבנן banned the blowing to protect against this.

keyTerms.meaning: Experts; people who know how to do something properly
A rabbinic decree made to prevent a violation
Lest; in case
Four cubits; the distance that makes carrying forbidden
The public domain

phrases.english: For Rabba said:
All are obligated in blowing the shofar,
but not all are experts in blowing the shofar;
it is a decree, lest one take it in his hand
and go to the expert to learn,
and carry it four cubits
in the public domain.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the reasoning behind the rabbinic decree that רבא mentioned in Step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The רבנן forbade blowing the שופר on שבת for fear that someone would carry it four אמות in the public domain on the way to learn from an expert.

steps.title: The same reason applies to לולב and מגילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that this same concern about carrying is why we do not take the לולב or read the מגילה on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is the reason for the לולב, and this is the reason for the מגילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא extends רבה's reason to two other מצוות that are pushed off when they fall on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the שופר, the לולב and the מגילה need know-how, so a person might carry them to an expert. That is why the רבנן also forbade taking the לולב and reading the מגילה on שבת. One decree, one reason, three מצוות.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is the same reason
The palm branch taken on סוכות
מגילת אסתר, read on פורים

steps.whatToRemember: Blowing the שופר on שבת is allowed by Torah law. The רבנן forbade it because of the fear of carrying in רשות הרבים, and the same decree applies to לולב and מגילה.

phrases.english: And this is the reason for the lulav,
and this is the reason for the Megillah.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְלוּלָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבה's reasoning from Step 14 to other cases.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The fear of carrying to an expert is the shared reason the רבנן forbade שופר, לולב, and מגילה on שבת.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's enactment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה: after the בית המקדש was destroyed, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי made an enactment about blowing the שופר on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: After the בית המקדש was destroyed, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי enacted, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה so it can explain it with a ברייתא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that after the חורבן, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי ruled that the שופר may be blown on שבת wherever there is a בית דין. Since the ban is only rabbinic, as we just learned, it makes sense that a בית דין could be treated like the מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: After the Temple was destroyed
He enacted; made a rabbinic ruling or institution
Etc.; the quote continues in the משנה

phrases.english: After the Temple was destroyed

phrases.aramaic: הִתְקִין רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai instituted, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשֶּׁחָרַב בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ הִתְקִין רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new section by quoting the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the חורבן, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי enacted that the שופר be blown on שבת in places with a בית דין.

steps.title: The story: ראש השנה on שבת in יבנה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells how ראש השנה once fell on שבת. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי told the בני בתירא, 'Let us blow!' and they answered, 'Let us discuss it first.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: once ראש השנה fell on שבת and all the towns gathered. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי said to the בני בתירא, 'Let us blow!' They said to him, 'Let us discuss it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that tells the background story of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's enactment. The story continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people gathered in יבנה, where the סנהדרין sat after the חורבן. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי wanted to blow right away, as in the מקדש. The בני בתירא, the leaders of the time, wanted to first discuss whether it was allowed. The answer to their request comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן taught; introduces a ברייתא
Were gathering together
The sons of Beseira, leading Torah authorities of that time
Let us blow
Let us discuss or debate the matter

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Once Rosh Hashanah occurred
on Shabbat,
and all the towns were gathering.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי לִבְנֵי בְּתִירָה:
phrases.english: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai said to the sons of Beseira:
Let us blow!
They said to him: Let us discuss it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: פַּעַם אַחַת חָל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the historical background to the משנה quoted in Step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי pushed to blow the שופר in יבנה on שבת, while the בני בתירא wanted to discuss it first.

steps.title: Blow first, discuss later
steps.stepSummary: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי answers the בני בתירא: first we blow, and afterward we will discuss it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Let us blow, and afterward we will discuss.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues the story. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי answers the בני בתירא's request to discuss first by saying they should blow first and discuss later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בני בתירא wanted a debate before acting. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי reverses the order: the action comes first and the discussion second. This sets up the clever ending in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us blow (the שופר)
Let us discuss / debate
The family of sages who led before רבן יוחנן בן זכאי

phrases.english: He said to them: Let us blow,
and afterward we will discuss.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: נִתְקַע, וְאַחַר כָּךְ נָדוּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 17 with רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's reply.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שופר is blown first, and the discussion comes afterward.

steps.title: The שופר was already heard, so the matter is closed
steps.stepSummary: After the blowing, the בני בתירא ask to discuss. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי replies that the שופר has already been heard in יבנה, and one does not argue against something already done.
steps.simpleTranslation: After they blew, they said to him: Let us discuss! He said to them: The horn has already been heard in יבנה, and we do not argue against something after it has been done.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. When the בני בתירא try to hold the debate, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי says it is too late: the practice has already been carried out publicly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the שופר was already blown in יבנה, a precedent now exists. The rule "אין משיבין לאחר מעשה" means a completed public act is not challenged afterward. In this way the enactment became established.

keyTerms.meaning: Horn (the שופר)
Yavne, the seat of the סנהדרין after the חורבן
We do not argue against an act once it has been done

steps.whatToRemember: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי set up the practice of blowing on שבת in יבנה by doing it first. Once it was done, it was no longer open for debate.

phrases.english: After they blew,
they said to him: Let us discuss!
He said to them:
The horn has already been heard in Yavne,
and we do not argue after the deed is done.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּבָר נִשְׁמְעָה קֶרֶן בְּיַבְנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the story of the ברייתא begun in step 17 and continued in step 18.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Once the שופר was blown in יבנה, the enactment stood, and the debate could not be reopened.

steps.title: Only in יבנה, or anywhere with a court
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: רבי אלעזר says the enactment was only for יבנה, and the חכמים say it applies in יבנה and in any place with a בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי made the enactment only in יבנה. They said to him: It applies both in יבנה and in any place that has a בית דין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה. That line records a disagreement about where blowing on שבת is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר limits the enactment to the one city of יבנה. The חכמים answer that it applies wherever there is a בית דין. This sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who limits the enactment to יבנה
Enacted / instituted
Rabbinic court

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הִתְקִין רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
phrases.english: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai did not institute it
except in Yavne alone.
They said to him:
Both Yavne and

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ בֵּית דִּין.
phrases.english: any place that has a court.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: לֹא הִתְקִין רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי אֶלָּא בְּיַבְנֶה בִּלְבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the ברייתא, the גמרא returns to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר says the enactment applies only in יבנה. The חכמים say it applies in any place with a בית דין.

steps.title: Isn't that just the first opinion again?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges that the חכמים' reply sounds identical to the opening statement of the משנה, the תנא קמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Their statement "They said to him" is the same as the תנא קמא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the משנה bothers to record the חכמים' answer. The משנה already said at the start that blowing is done in any place with a בית דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה opened by saying רבן יוחנן בן זכאי enacted blowing in every place with a בית דין. The חכמים' reply seems to repeat exactly that. A משנה does not normally repeat itself, so the גמרא expects there to be some difference.

keyTerms.meaning: That is the same as
The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Here "אמרו לו" is not the חכמים speaking again. The גמרא is quoting the words of the משנה to name the statement it is asking about.

phrases.english: "They said to him": that is the same as the first tanna!
phrases.notes: "אמרו לו" is a citation of the משנה's words.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ תַּנָּא קַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the משנה quoted in step 20 includes the חכמים' reply at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים' reply to רבי אלעזר in the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Their view seems identical to the תנא קמא, so recording it again looks unnecessary.

steps.title: The difference: a temporary court
steps.stepSummary: The two views differ over a temporary בית דין. The תנא קמא allows blowing there too, while the חכמים require a permanent court like יבנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is a temporary בית דין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two opinions are not identical. They disagree about a בית דין that sits in a place only temporarily.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the תנא קמא, any בית דין, even a temporary one, allows blowing on שבת. According to the חכמים who answered רבי אלעזר, only a fixed, permanent בית דין counts, similar to the one in יבנה. So each statement adds a distinct position.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them
A temporary court, not fixed in one place

steps.whyThisMatters: It tells us the halachic reach of the enactment: whether a non-permanent court is enough for blowing on שבת.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them:
a temporary court.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ בֵּי דִינָא דְּאַקְרַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a practical difference (נפקא מינה) between the two opinions.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים simply repeat the תנא קמא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא קמא includes a temporary court, while the חכמים require a permanent court like יבנה.

steps.title: רב הונא comments on the Sages' line
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the חכמים' statement again to introduce a comment by רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Both in יבנה and in any place that has a בית דין. רב הונא said:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא re-quotes the חכמים' words from the משנה because רב הונא is about to explain them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The repetition is not redundant. It marks a new topic: what רב הונא has to say about this line. His actual statement follows on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who comments on the משנה

phrases.english: They said to him:
Both Yavne and

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ בֵּית דִּין.
phrases.english: any place that has a court.
Rav Huna said:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אֶחָד יַבְנֶה וְאֶחָד כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ בֵּית דִּין. אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Re-quotes the line from step 20 to begin a new discussion led by רב הונא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces רב הונא's explanation of the חכמים' statement, which continues on the next amud.
